title: Arbitration and Conciliation Act s. 27 — Statutory provision (ACA s. 27)

content.overview: Section 27 permits the arbitral tribunal, or a party with tribunal approval, to apply to the Court for assistance in taking evidence. The statutory mechanism governs the application, service and execution of the evidentiary process through the Court.
content.glance: Section 27 permits the arbitral tribunal, or a party with tribunal approval, to apply to the Court for assistance in taking evidence. The statutory mechanism governs the application, service and execution of the evidentiary process through the Court.
content.study:
Section 27 — Court assistance in taking evidence

Section 27 permits the arbitral tribunal, or a party with tribunal approval, to apply to the Court for assistance in taking evidence. The statutory mechanism governs the application, service and execution of the evidentiary process through the Court.

The provision must be applied by identifying its operative conditions, the procedural stage and its connected sections. Statutory exceptions and party agreements must be kept distinct from the default rule.
